text: If two triangles have  two sides equal to two sides, respectively,  and also have the base equal to the base, then they will also have equal the angles  encompassed by the equal straight-lines.      Let $ABC$ and $DEF$ be two triangles having the two sides $AB$ and $AC$ equal to the two sides $DE$ and $DF$, respectively. (That is) $AB$ to $DE$, and $AC$ to $DF$.  Let them also have the base $BC$ equal to the base $EF$. I say that the angle $BAC$ is also equal to the angle $EDF$.

For if triangle $ABC$ is applied to triangle $DEF$, the point $B$ being placed on point $E$, and the straight-line $BC$ on $EF$, then point $C$ will also coincide with $F$, on account of $BC$ being equal to $EF$.
assertion: when triangle ABC is applied to triangle DEF with B on E and BC on EF, point C coincides with F

text: So  (because of) $BC$ coinciding with $EF$,  (the sides) $BA$ and $CA$ will also coincide with  $ED$ and $DF$ (respectively).
assertion: sides BA and CA coincide with ED and DF respectively

text: For if base $BC$ coincides with base $EF$, but the sides $AB$ and $AC$  do not coincide with $ED$ and $DF$ (respectively), but miss like $EG$ and $GF$ (in the above figure),
assertion: reductio hypothesis: the sides AB and AC do not coincide with ED and DF (they miss at G)

text: then we will have constructed upon the same straight-line, two other straight-lines equal, respectively, to two (given) straight-lines,
assertion: two other straight-lines, on the same base, equal respectively to the two given straight-lines

text: and (meeting) at a different point on the same side (of the straight-line),
assertion: meeting at a different point on the same side

text: Thus,  the base $BC$ being applied to the  base $EF$,  the sides $BA$ and $AC$ cannot not coincide with $ED$ and $DF$ (respectively).
assertion: the sides BA and AC cannot fail to coincide with ED and DF

text: So the angle $BAC$ will also coincide with angle $EDF$, and will be equal to it [C.N.~4].
assertion: angle BAC coincides with angle EDF and is equal to it

text: Thus, if two triangles have  two  sides equal to two side, respectively, and  have the base equal to the base, then they will also have equal the angles  encompassed by the equal straight-lines. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
